text:
maria: Proposal — we should standardize where trace_id is attached to logs. I'm seeing multiple ad-hoc fields (`trace_id`, `trace`, `x_trace`) across services which makes joins in the console brittle. Thoughts?
aj: agree. big problem in dashboards + alerts. sometimes trace is only in HTTP header so logs miss it.
ryan: curious: do we want to require apps to emit a structured `trace.trace_id` field, or enrich at the log-forwarder/collector? tradeoffs: accuracy vs integration burden.
sophia: my +1 to collector enrichment for legacy services. collector sees both OTLP spans and logs and can attach span.trace_id when both present.
maria: collector enrichment works when logs and spans are routed together and come close in time. we have out-of-order delivery and batching — sometimes collector gets logs first without span context.
aj: exactly — we had a replay where logs landed hours before spans (async exporters). then enrichment is impossible.
ryan: alternative: SDK-level contract: add `redwood.trace_id` (or `trace_id`) to structured logs if present in context. tiny change in our JSON logger wrappers.
sophia: SDK change is ideal for new code, but slow to roll out. hybrid approach: SDK adds field when available; collector uses heuristics and header fallbacks (`traceparent`, `X-Cloud-Trace-Context`) to attach when missing.
maria: ok but we need a canonical field name and type. proposal: `trace_id` (lowercase, hex string) at top-level in JSON logs. also permit `trace.parent_id` for span id compatibility.
aj: +1 for simpler `trace_id` top-level — easier for ES/BigQuery field mapping and dashboards.
ryan: what about sampling? if we don't send spans for sampled-out traces, collector can't enrich. Should we propagate sampled-out trace IDs in logs anyway? That could affect cardinality.
sophia: we can add `trace_sampled: true|false` (boolean) to logs. that keeps metadata consistent. retention/cost note: trace_id is high-cardinality but already present in spans. logs with trace_id will spike cardinality in indexing (ES fields). need to document retention impact.
maria: downstream effects: dashboards that count traces vs logs must dedupe by trace_id. also need alerting queries to use `trace_id` where present.
aj: ops ask: we must strip PII — is trace_id PII? no. but full request IDs that encode user info could be. we should add a linter that blocks keys like `user.email` in logs.
ryan: implementation plan:
1) platform -> specify schema: top-level `trace_id`, optional `trace_parent_id`, optional `trace_sampled`.
2) SDKs -> add a small logger wrapper to include trace_id from context when present.
3) Collector -> add OTLP pipeline enrich step that looks for `traceparent`/headers and span store; attach if SDK missed.
4) Docs -> update Console linking docs and dashboards to use `trace_id` for joins.

sophia: collector config prototype (OpenTelemetry Collector):
```
processors:
  trace_enricher:
    lookup_span_store: true

service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, trace_enricher]
      exporters: [redwood_ingest]
```

aj: question for security: where do we keep the small span lookup store? in-memory LRU in collector pods? TTL probably 30s-5m depending on ordering.
maria: keep TTL small by default (30s) and make it config per environment. long-tail reorders can be handled by SDK approach.
ryan: will create PR to platform spec doc for `trace_id` field. tagging @sre for retention impact and @devex for SDK changes.
maria: thanks — @sre can you run a quick estimate for index size impact if we add trace_id to logs for high-traffic endpoints? also propose a canary rollout (10% of services) and metrics to watch: index size growth, query latency, dashboard joins correctness.
sre-bot: perf-estimate task created: INFRA-4837
sre-bot: added assignees: glen, priya
priya: will run rough numbers today, but initial thought: if trace_id stored as keyword in ES it will increase shards' doc values size. possible mitigation: store as ephemeral field not indexed, use doc join on ingest pipeline? need to evaluate.
maria: cool — next step rk: I'll open the spec PR and drop the logger change snippet. thanks all.
